LESSON: READING ALOUD PHRASING ARTICULATION WORD RECOGNITION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: FRENCH
Strand: Reading 2.5 Reading for Understanding Vocabulary Chunking Word recognition By th
Topic 2.7: Reading Aloud Phrasing Articulation Word recognition

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading Aloud Phrasing Articulation Word recognition. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do you ensure you read without tension?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read texts with correct intonation, pace, and fluency
2. read varied texts with enthusiasm

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING ALOUD PHRASING ARTICULATION WORD RECOGNITION
Subject: FRENCH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading Aloud Phrasing Articulation Word recognition helps you succeed in FRENCH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING ALOUD PHRASING ARTICULATION WORD RECOGNITION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read texts with correct intonation, pace, and fluency

What this means
In this part you learn to read texts with correct intonation, pace, and fluency. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read texts with correct intonation, pace, and fluency.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading Aloud Phrasing Articulation Word recognition”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read texts with correct intonation, pace, and fluency. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Read varied texts with enthusiasm

What this means
In this part you learn to read varied texts with enthusiasm. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read varied texts with enthusiasm.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading Aloud Phrasing Articulation Word recognition to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read varied texts with enthusiasm. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading Aloud Phrasing Articulation Word recognition is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading Aloud Phrasing Articulation Word recognition”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read texts with correct intonation, pace, and fluency)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading Aloud Phrasing Articulation Word recognition to a partner. (skill: read varied texts with enthusiasm)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading Aloud Phrasing Articulation Word recognition to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read texts with correct intonation, pace, and fluency.
3. Practise this skill: read varied texts with enthusiasm.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading Aloud Phrasing Articulation Word recognition from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading Aloud Phrasing Articulation Word recognition: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Reading Aloud Phrasing Articulation Word recognition?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you ensure you read without tension?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading Aloud Phrasing Articulation Word recognition means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read texts with correct intonation, pace, and fluency.
5. Be able to: read varied texts with enthusiasm.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
